bodies.intuition: A good learning rate early is a bad one late. Early on the model is far from anything useful and can take large steps; near the end it needs small ones to settle. A schedule moves the rate down over the run, usually along a cosine, so the same run gets both.
bodies.engineer: Cosine decay to near zero over the planned number of steps is the common default. The schedule is tied to the total length, so stopping early leaves the model at a rate it was never meant to finish at, and extending a run means the tail of the schedule has already been spent.
bodies.math: η_t = η_min + ½(η_max − η_min)(1 + cos(πt/T)) for total steps T. Because T appears in the formula, the trajectory for a run of length T is not a prefix of the trajectory for a longer one.
